primary_claim: Using a closed-form formula for expected mean-max-absolute-cosine-similarity of random unit vectors, the authors show that superposition interference grows extremely slowly with the number of concept vectors relative to dimensionality, such that 16k features in a 768-dim space (as used in SynthSAEBench-16k) produces more superposition interference (rho_mm = 0.14) than 10 trillion concepts in an 8192-dim space, and optimal vector placement offers negligible improvement over random placement in high dimensions.

effect.value: SynthSAEBench-16k (16k features, d=768): rho_mm = 0.14, more interference than 10 trillion concepts in d=8192 (Llama-3.1-70B hidden dim)

quote: 10 trillion concepts in 8192 dimensions has far less superposition interference than just 100K concepts in 768 dimensions (the hidden dimension of GPT-2)!
